months.1: The northeast monsoon delivers consistent windswell to the northern tip of Sabah. Beginners and longboarders find fun 2-4 ft waves on the sandy beach breaks near Kudat, with water warm enough to surf without a wetsuit.

borabora.overview: French Polynesia is famous for Teahupo'o on Tahiti's southeast coast, a world-reference, heavy left-hand reef break strictly for experts. Most breaks here are shallow, razor-sharp reefs requiring a boat to access. The prime season runs from May to September when powerful south swells hit. While experts chase massive barrels, beginners have very few options, limited to a couple of beach breaks like Papara. The water is warm enough to surf without a wetsuit year-round.

months.6: Peak season for south and southwest swells. Teahupo'o fires with world-reference, heavy left-hand barrels that can reach 10-15 ft on big days. This is strictly expert territory over a dangerous, shallow reef accessed by boat. The water is 77 F, so no wetsuit is needed.

big-island.overview: The Big Island has real surf, though it is quieter than the world-famous breaks of Oahu or Maui. Honoli'i on the east side is a river mouth break for intermediates and experts, while Kahalu'u on the Kona side offers a beginner-friendly reef. Winter brings larger swells to exposed coasts, but the island's rocky shoreline and trade winds mean finding the right spot takes some local knowledge. The water is warm enough to surf without a wetsuit year-round.

months.2: North Pacific winter swells continue to deliver consistent 4-8 ft waves to exposed shores. Experts and intermediates can find power at Honoli'i, while beginners stick to the sheltered reef at Kahalu'u. No wetsuit is needed in the 76°F water.

months.7: Summer means smaller, gentler waves, ideal for beginners at the Zarautz beach break. Wave faces are typically 2-4 ft. The water reaches 68-72°F, comfortable in a 3/2 mm wetsuit. The expert river mouth at Mundaka rarely breaks.

bali.overview: Bali is a legendary surf destination with world-class reef breaks on the Bukit Peninsula and miles of beginner-friendly beach breaks. Experts travel for the heavy, hollow lefts at Uluwatu and Padang Padang, which fire during the dry season (April to October). Beginners and intermediates find softer waves at Kuta and Canggu year-round. The water is 79-84°F, so no wetsuit is needed, but the famous reefs are shallow, sharp, and often crowded.

aruba.overview: Aruba is better known for wind sports, but experienced surfers can find shortboard waves on the rugged north and east coasts. Breaks like Andicuri pick up winter swells and trade wind chop. Strong currents, rocky entries, and no surf schools make it unsuitable for beginners.

months.1: North Atlantic swells bring 3-5 ft waves to rocky north coast breaks like Andicuri. The water is 80 F, so no wetsuit is needed, but experts must navigate strong currents and sharp rocks.
